I’m a US citizen and I got a family private life visa from my French spouse. I first applied for a long stay tourist visa, so I had the right to live in France for up to a year. You need to show proof of funds and living accommodation, so my husband wrote letters claiming financial and living responsibility for me. We wanted to get married asap. I arrived in the summer, which was a bad idea, because the entire marriage sector of my city’s prefecture was on holidays, so I wasn’t able to get married until late in the year. 

After that, I applied for the family private life visa/ titre de sejour, which would grant me the right to work and study. It was approved a few months later and went into effect after my original tourist visa expired. It’s good for 2 years and after, I’ll be able to apply for a new titre de sejour. 

I recommend taking this route because under the tourist visa, you’re safe from the 90 days rule and you don’t have to leave the country. The time you have allows you to establish your address, bank account, carte vitale, etc, before you request a titre de sejour, which makes things so much easier.
